{{Short description|American statistician}}

'''Barry Robert Davis''' is an American statistician and public health doctor specializing in the design, conduct, and analysis of [[clinical trials]].<ref name="auto1">{{cite web | url=https://sph.uth.edu/faculty/index.htm#CPA+A3xTAYs1b2zCbfWgSQ== | title=Faculty }}</ref> He is Professor Emeritus of [[Biostatistics]] and [[Data science|Data Science]] at the University of Texas School of Public Health, where he served as Director of its Coordinating Center for Clinical Trials.<ref name="auto1"/> He served as President of the Society for Clinical Trials in 2000<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.sctweb.org/presidents.cfm | title=Society for Clinical Trials }}</ref> and as Chair of the Biometrics Section of the [[American Statistical Association]] in 2003.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://community.amstat.org/biometricsbiom/home | title=ASA Community }}</ref>

==Education and career==

Davis earned a B.S. degree from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1973.,<ref name="auto1"/> an M.D. from the [[University of California, San Diego, School of Medicine]],<ref name="auto1"/> and a Ph.D. in [[Applied mathematics|Applied Mathematics]] under the supervision of [[Stuart Geman]] in the Division of Applied Mathematics at [[Brown University]] in 1982, based on his dissertation entitled "A Neurobiological Approach to Machine Intelligence."<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=14549 | title=Barry Davis - the Mathematics Genealogy Project }}</ref> He joined the Division of Applied Mathematics at Brown University as an assistant professor in 1982 and moved in 1983 to the University of Texas School of Public Health where he ultimately was the Guy S. Parcel Chair of Public Health, Professor of Biostatistics and Data Science, and Director of the Coordinating Center for Clinical Trials.<ref name="auto1"/>

Davis had leadership roles in four influential hypertension clinical trials: the Hypertension Detection and Follow-up Program (HDFP),<ref>{{cite book |last=Black |first=Henry R. |editor-link=Henry R. Black (editor) |date=2001 |title=Clinical Trials in Hypertension |url= |location=Boca Raton, Florida |publisher=CRC Press |pages=27–60 |isbn=978-0-824-70270-0}}</ref> the Systolic Hypertension in the Elderly Program (SHEP),<ref>{{cite book |last=Black |first=Henry R. |editor-link=Henry R. Black (editor)|date=2001 |title=Clinical Trials in Hypertension |url= |location=Boca Raton, Florida |publisher=CRC Press |pages=195–232 |isbn=978-0-824-70270-0}}</ref> the [[Antihypertensive and Lipid Lowering Treatment to Prevent Heart Attack Trial]] (ALLHAT) <ref>{{cite book |last=Black |first=Henry R. |editor-link= Henry R. Black (editor)|date=2001 |title=Clinical Trials in Hypertension |url= |location=Boca Raton, Florida |publisher=CRC Press |pages=531–586 |isbn=978-0-824-70270-0}}</ref><ref name="Davis1996">{{cite journal |last1=Davis |first1=Barry R.|last2=Cutler| first2=JA | last3=Gordon|first3=DJ |last4= et | first4= al. |title=Rationale and design of the Antihypertensive and Lipid Lowering Treatment to Prevent Heart Attack Trial (ALLHAT). | journal=Am J Hypertens |date= 1 April 1996 |volume=9 |issue=4 |pages=342–360 |doi=10.1016/0895-7061(96)00037-4 |pmid=8722437 |doi-access=free }}</ref> and the Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT); <ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.nejm.org/doi/suppl/10.1056/NEJMoa1511939/suppl_file/nejmoa1511939_appendix.pdf|doi=10.1056/NEJMoa1511939|title=A Randomized Trial of Intensive versus Standard Blood-Pressure Control|journal=New England Journal of Medicine|year=2015|volume=373|issue=22|pages=2103–2116|pmid=26551272|author1=SPRINT Research Group|last2=Wright Jr|first2=J. T.|last3=Williamson|first3=J. D.|last4=Whelton|first4=P. K.|last5=Snyder|first5=J. K.|last6=Sink|first6=K. M.|last7=Rocco|first7=M. V.|last8=Reboussin|first8=D. M.|last9=Rahman|first9=M.|last10=Oparil|first10=S.|last11=Lewis|first11=C. E.|last12=Kimmel|first12=P. L.|last13=Johnson|first13=K. C.|last14=Goff Jr|first14=D. C.|last15=Fine|first15=L. J.|last16=Cutler|first16=J. A.|last17=Cushman|first17=W. C.|last18=Cheung|first18=A. K.|last19=Ambrosius|first19=W. T.|pmc=4689591}}</ref> and in stem cell therapy trials for treating heart disease, the [[Cardiovascular Cell Therapy Research Network]].

==Recognition==

Davis became a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 1996, a Fellow of the Society for Clinical Trials in 2007, a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2014 for "distinguished contributions to the methodology of clinical trials; the design, monitoring, management, and reporting of influential clinical trials; and leadership to advance public health",<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.fda.gov/media/129500/download |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210306203542/https://www.fda.gov/media/129500/download |archive-date=2021-03-06 |access-date=2025-10-19 |website=www.fda.gov}}</ref> and an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]] in 2015.<ref>{{cite web| url= https://www.isi-web.org/about/members/individual| title= ISA Elected Member| access-date= 2022-09-23| archive-date= 2022-09-23| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220923155438/https://www.isi-web.org/about/members/individual| url-status= dead}}</ref> In 2004 he received the University of Texas Health President's Scholar's Award for his leadership role in the ALLHAT Clinical Trial.<ref>{{cite web|author=Office of Faculty Affairs and Development |url=https://www.uth.edu/ofad/psa/list-of-awardees |title=List of Awardees - President's Scholar Awards - Office of Faculty Affairs and Development - UTHealth |publisher=Uth.edu |date=2022-04-14 |accessdate=2022-09-23}}</ref> He is also a Fellow of the [[American Heart Association]], the [[American Society of Hypertension]], and the [[American College of Preventive Medicine]].<ref name="auto"/>
